pr_body:
Closes #14471 

The fix for the exception in the linked issue was to define a `DifficultyBindableWithCurrent` that inherits from `DifficultyBindable` but has similar logic to `BindableWithCurrent`, instead of using `BindableWithCurrent` directly and binding it to `DifficultyBindable`s which caused that exception.

I've also refactored `DifficultyAdjustSettingsControl` a touch to not be required to implement a weird `float? Current` bindable in the underlying slider control, and simplified a bit of things in result thanks to the implemented `DifficultyBindable.BindTo` logic that allows it.

Note that the reason the `UnbindFrom` exception in the mentioned issue thread doesn't appear without a debugger is because `Drawable` intentionally catches exceptions and doesn't perform any actions about them, with the comment "Execution should continue regardless of whether an unbind failed".

https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/blob/bcf1047e981e40cdfc63233b5a0fdd7f5eeac832/osu.Framework/Graphics/Drawable.cs#L146-L159

---

I've tested all the possible scenarios I can think of (solo and multiplayer) just to make sure there are no regressions, and everything looks to be alright.
pr_comments:
The original description doesn't seem to have fully expressed the intention of this PR, so I'll rewrite it here just to make everything clear, because there's actually no sane way to have the simple fix without refactoring it to what I currently have:

The simple fix, as mentioned above, is to make a `DifficultyAdjustWithCurrent` bindable class that's similar to `BindableWithCurrent`.

But applying that fix alone would make the whole control end up reading weirdly in general, and questions would start to be raised, such as:
 1. Why is there a `GetBoundCopy()` call in `DifficultyAdjustSettingsControl.Current` while it's going to get bound to again in `SliderControl.Current`.
 2. Why is there even a `DifficultyBindableWithCurrent` inside a `SliderControl` itself while it's going to completely ignore it and use a different bindable provided in constructor.
 3. Why are the members in `DifficultyBindableWithCurrent` instance such as `CurrentNumber` left unused while they're instantiated and properly bound to their sources, meaning that they could be benefical in replacement to the current `sliderDisplayCurrent` and the way it's bound.

All of these questions I've started to notice made me rewrite the whole control a bit to make it look more saner and actually make sense of how it's implemented, and not waste bindable instances and copies.

I've first started by allowing `SettingsItem`s to be able to provide custom implementation for `SettingsItem.Current` and not have to implement the same matching `IHasCurrentValue<T>` in their underlying control, that's to allow removing the weird `Current` bindable in `SliderControl` which looks to be ignored yet still used in a roundabout way.

So now `DifficultyAdjustSettingsControl` owns the `DifficultyBindableWithCurrent` instead and be able to use it properly, rather than obtaining a copy instance while another goes inside `SliderControl`.

Then, after looking at `DifficultyBindableWithCurrent` and the `DifficultyBindable.BindTo` logic, I noticed I can completely remove the "intercepting" part of `DifficultyAdjustSettingsControl.Current` and the `sliderDisplayCurrent` bindable by instead using the `DifficultyBindableWithCurrent`'s `CurrentNumber` bindable directly, which gets correctly bound to the source difficutly bindable on `Current` set.

I've also then renamed `CurrentNumber` to `DisplayBindable` so that it doesn't conflict with the known naming of "`Current`", also didn't choose to use `Constraints` in the naming because really the whole bindable gets fully used in the slider, so it doesn't make sense to name it that way. (I guess the xmldoc meant not setting it in initialization usages, could be reworded)

comments: Can't repro on the latest release, so either a regression or more to it.
Can't reproduce on master, could you please provide more exact steps?

I'm seeing the same issue on the release commit (d3dba296d672afa4d5c4d7c97154fe68117935a1) with these exact steps:
- build and launch game (via vscode debug configuration)
- click osu logo -> play -> solo
- open mod menu with f1
- scroll down and select difficulty adjust.
- deselect difficulty adjust
- Exception has occurred: CLR/System.InvalidOperationException

I think this is something your end.

Please test on an actual release binary.
Works as expected on the release binary.
I'd say you have some outdated dependencies. Please try updating nuget and potentially doing a full clean of the project / your IDE to ensure nothing is being cached in a bad state.

Another possibility is that you have a ruleset loaded which is doing something globally it shouldn't be doing. If so, please check rulesets one by one and let us know which this is so we can report upstream.

I managed to repro this in a testing scenario, no idea how/why but leaving this here:

![20210824 132713 (JetBrains Rider)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/130555806-bbd4dff8-b166-4770-b51d-be6947179f71.png)

I don't have much knowledge of why this exception exists so asking someone else to look into this.
Something is catching the exception blindly. This only reproduces with a debugger attached and set to break on all exceptions.

review_comments: I'm not sure this is named any better than it was previously. Maybe something like `CurrentConstraints` or `BindableConstraints` would work better. But this is all really quite out of scope.

Now that I look at it again actually, perhaps `CurrentNumber` is fine either way. Note that I didn't use `Constraints` as the bindable gets fully used in the slider either way, so it doesn't make sense to bind a slider to a "constraints" bindable rather than a "current" or "display".

I'll revert the naming after https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/14478#discussion_r695051162 gets settled, as which to use would depend on how that should be dealt with.

What purpose does this serve? Can the usages of this use `current.DisplayBindable` directly, rather than going through one more layer of indirection (accompanied by one more confusing name to grasp, to boot)?

Just to make it clear in usages that `current.DisplayBindable` is the slider bindable, with the name `DisplayBindable`, I think it won't be that confusing to inline it in usages, but not sure if I were to revert it to `CurrentNumber`

I do not think this change is desirable. So now, apparently, `Current` - which is *integral* to this setting stuff working properly - can throw in runtime, and despite that `SliderControl` willingly doesn't implement `IHasCurrentValue` for a single edge-case mod? That seems backwards. If that exception ever trips, it will look like an actual oversight rather than a deliberate choice (i.e. that it should be implementing `IHasCurrentValue` but someone forgot to do it).

Not sure what your point is? I don't see how it's backwards to actually implement a `DifficultyBindable` current inside `SliderControl` itself, if it's gonna completely ignore it there and use a different bindable, that's the opposite to me.

The point is that while this change does remove the bindable passing, it does so at the expense of willingly bypassing the core structure of how settings controls work. Which is not unequivocally better for me - more like slightly below par when compared with the current version.

The actual clean way to get rid of the bindable passing would be by having a bindable number type supporting nullable types.

Having nullable type support that displays a default in case of null would make things even more clean, the way done in this PR is to have an intermediate mapping between a `DifficultyBindable` and a `BindableNumber<float>`, as in below:
https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/cd2556bd110576e639c5ca4fc3c0c23a8bd46e6e/osu.Game/Rulesets/Mods/DifficultyAdjustSettingsControl.cs#L24-L39

And as I've mentioned, reverting back to just the simple fix makes the control in general read weirdly, but I'll wait to hear more opinions. (for example, here's how it would look if I were to apply the simple fix alone, for cross comparsion https://github.com/ppy/osu/compare/master...frenzibyte:alternative-difficulty-bindable?expand=1)
I'm not completely against this change, but wouldn't it make more sense to move the exception / whatever to trigger after `CreateControl` is run? In fact, that's how it's done on `master`?

But `CreateControl` is allowed to return a type that's not `IHasCurrentValue`, it's the implementation of `Current` that would decide whether to throw or not, if `Current` wasn't overriden and reached the `SettingsItem`'s implementation, then throw the exception if not implemented `IHasCurrentValue`.

overridden current sounds like a really bad pattern in the first place. i'd look to remove that via some means, if possible.

note that i'm saying this without looking too deep into the issue. feel free to fire back as to why this is not feasible or warranted.

If I were to remove the override pattern and let `SliderControl` have the current bindable implementation instead (`float?` one), there'll be no way to access the `DifficultyBindable` from the main control itself without fetching it from the slider control, and that feels really awkward in code readability to me. (unless we still override `Current` to save an instance of the `DifficultyBindable` before setting `base.Current`, making us jump into bindable reference issues because `Drawable` would unbind it on disposal)

The simple variant linked above looks vastly preferable to me. I have zero issues with it and I don't follow how it would make any of the existing code read any worse _than it already does_.

If the concern is about code quality then you'd have to take a detour of a few pulls to start getting the difficulty bindable stuff in better shape. I consider the "code quality" changes in this pull mostly _orthogonal_ (i.e. some problems are "solved", but new ones are introduced in exchange).

Are there really new problems introduced here other than the `Current` override and the allowing of having settings controls without `IHasCurrentValue` (in exchange for overriding `Current` and connecting it to the underlying control in some form, i.e. "custom implementation")?
Allowing settings controls to not implement `IHasCurrentValue` is literally the biggest problem I have with this diff right now.
I don't think this is gonna be easily solvable then, I'll proceed with closing this PR and going with the simple fix alone if no one has any other opinions on the matter.
The proposed solution looks far better.
